inventory_summary: Probed all 184 resolved walls' members: stud/plate heights vs storey stack, header vs plates, 90 openings' kings/jacks/headers, stud gaps off module, takeoff stock lengths; read S-601 and A-503. Time-limited: corner packs, stagger studs, A-532..552 and S-101/103 sheets not examined in detail. Second pass: corners, staggered walls, S-101.1, S-103.2/.3, A-532, A-544 examined; S-101.2/.3, S-103.1/.4 and the other A-5xx details not individually viewed.
verified_clean: All framed walls: stud top = bottom of lowest top plate and stud bottom = sole plate top (stack continuous, no gaps), main/second 103.5 in. ext (108 in. plates), partitions 102.875 (107.375 top, deliberate 3/4 in. clear per CLAUDE.md), basement/garage consistent
Actual lumber dims: 2x4=1.5x3.5, 2x6=1.5x5.5, 2x8 7.25, 2x10 9.25 in headers; LVL header depths exact (9.5, 14, 5.5)
Jack inner faces land on RO edge (e.g. 38.24 in. RO: jack centre 19.87 in. = 19.12+0.75) with kings packed outboard, jack bottoms on sole plate, tops on header bottom
Every header except D-G-SERVICE and D-B-PATIO tops below the lowest top plate (p14.py)
Window RO jamb packs 27.5/30 in.: 1 king+1 jack per side, header 2-2x8 sits at RO head; no stud/jack stacking conflicts
Garage walls frame at 24 in. o.c. (2x6, 95.5 in. studs) as designed; W-B/W-M partition gaps only at doors/walls ends
R602.7.5 jack/king table not independently verified (ICC site 403, web search inconclusive)

Corners (W-M/W-S S1,E1,N1,W1B): 4-stud corner = end stud + two corner studs on the owner wall (2x6, z 1.5..105/121.5..225) with the neighbour's end stud butting; sizes true 1.5x5.5, heights match the stack, corner studs billed as lsl on main

Staggered walls (W-M-LS, W-M-HS1): 2x4 studs at +/-1.0 in. off axis on a 2x6 plate (flush to alternating plate faces, 3.5 in. in a 5.5 in. plate), 16 in. o.c. per face / 8 in. along, 2x6 end studs; plate profile 2x6 as per memory
S-103.2/.3 panel labels vs braced_walls.py: east main 34/43/154 = 34.25/42.75/153.5; second S1 six 32-34 in. runs total ~16.7 ft vs PROV 16.78

findings.title: D-G-SERVICE header runs 2 in. up into the garage double top plate

evidence.measured: header-0 3-1.75x5.5 LVL z 81.5..87.0; plate-top-1 z 85.0..86.5 and plate-top-0 86.5..88.0; kings/studs stop at 85.0. Header overlaps plate-top-1 fully and 0.5 in. of plate-top-0 (RO head 81.5 + 5.5 in. = 87 vs 85 framing height).
evidence.expected: Header top <= 85.0 (underside of lower top plate), or plates notched/header replaces the lower plate with a stated detail.
evidence.method: Probe: load_plan(houses/catlin)+resolve; scratchpad geometry-review/F1/p13.py, p14.py (header z1 > lowest top-plate z0 per wall). Wall W-G-S members within the opening station.

findings.source: IRC R602.7 (header sits under top plate); houses/catlin/CLAUDE.md garage plates 8'-4"
findings.proposed_fix: Shorten RO height (door RO 81.5 is derived from DT-EXT-SWING32-G; 79.5 max with a 5.5 in. header) or raise garage plate height; or drop plate-top-1 over the header and say so. Escalate: moves RO/plate height.

findings.title: D-B-PATIO liner header stands 1.6 in. above the framed liner wall top

evidence.measured: header-0 2-2x10 z -21.06..-11.81; plate-top-1 bottom -16.44, wall top -13.44. Header top is 4.6 in. into the plate zone and 1.63 in. above the wall top (basement ceiling/joist-bottom plane). RO height 82.88 + 9.25 in. header = 92.1 in. vs 84.25 in. stud height available.
evidence.expected: Header top <= -16.44 or the liner header omitted where the concrete/ICF opening above carries the load.
evidence.method: Probe: load_plan(houses/catlin)+resolve; scratchpad geometry-review/F1/p13.py, p14.py (header z1 > lowest top-plate z0 per wall). (HDR over plate list: W-B-S3-FR header-0).

findings.proposed_fix: Decide what carries load over D-B-PATIO in the garden liner; if the concrete does, frame a flat nailer only; else reduce RO or raise the liner wall.

findings.title: Plates over 20 ft ordered in non-stock lengths (22/28/36 ft) and never spliced

evidence.measured: framing_bom 2x6 plate stock: 3 x 36 ft, 1 x 28, 1 x 22, 11 x 24 (W-M-E1 plates are 35.46 ft cut). _order_length_ft rounds past 20 ft to next 2 ft; plates are not 'spliceable'.
evidence.expected: Dimension lumber stocked to 16/20 ft (24 ft special); plates are lap-spliced (4 ft min over a stud) in 12-20 ft sticks.
evidence.method: takeoff.json framing_bom; probe p15.py lists members > 20 ft.

findings.source: Local lumber yard stock; IRC R602.3.2 top-plate laps
findings.proposed_fix: Mark plate/raked_plate runs spliceable in _bucket_cut_lengths (cap 20 ft) with a lap allowance.

findings.title: W-S-W3 exterior wall drops module studs at 60 in. and 108 in. (32 in. bays)

evidence.measured: Studs at 12,13.5(jack),44,76,92,124,...: no stud at 60 or 108; bays 44-76 and 92-124 are 32 in. Truss blocks stand at 76 and 108 with no stud behind 108. All other second-storey facade walls keep 16 in. module.
evidence.expected: 16 in. o.c. stud line (module stations 28/44/60/76/92/108/124) except inside openings.
evidence.method: scratchpad F1/p9.py (gap > 16.3 in. outside openings), p10.py W-S-W3.

findings.source: IRC R602.3.1 (2x6 at 16 in. o.c. bearing); houses/catlin/CLAUDE.md ONE GRID PER FACADE
findings.proposed_fix: Find why the solver omitted stud-at-60/108 (continuation_roles seam owner at the W-S-W3/W-S-W2 tee? pocket?) and restore; confirm on S-101.2.

findings.title: W-M-PAN-S pocket-door header (74.5 in. 2-2x6) has no king/jack/end stud

evidence.measured: header-0 218.75..293.25 in. on a 79 in. wall; members: pocketsplit studs at 221/233/245, cripples at 273/289; no king/jack, no stud-000. Header ends 2.75 in. and 1.75 in. short of wall ends.
evidence.expected: Header ends bearing on kings/jacks or on the end-wall studs of the abutting walls.
evidence.method: scratchpad F1/p8.py. Low confidence: nonbearing partition, abutting walls may carry the ends.

findings.proposed_fix: Confirm intent; add end studs or document bearing on abutting walls.

findings.title: Stud heights are not precut stock lengths; ordered from 8/10 ft and cut

evidence.measured: Studs: main ext 103.5 in. (10 ft stock, 16.5 in. offcut each), partitions 102.875, basement 92.3125/91.5/90.75, garage 95.5. Precut studs are 92-5/8, 104-5/8, 116-5/8 (3-plate stack 4.5 in.).
evidence.expected: Plate stack 108 in. needs 103.5; precut 104-5/8 gives 109-1/8. Not a defect; BOM relies on field cutting.
evidence.method: scratchpad F1/p2.py, takeoff.json framing_bom stud rows.

findings.proposed_fix: Note in S-601/DESIGN-LOG that studs are cut from 10 ft stock; no geometry change.

findings.title: S-103.x braced-wall line summaries run off the sheet; code citations truncated

evidence.measured: BWL-W-A-E1/N1/S1/W1 result lines and the 'PANELS SHOWN ARE...' note are single unwrapped lines clipped at the right border: Table R602.10.3(1) text ends at 'Table R602.' / 'Table R6' and the R602.10.8 sentence ends mid-word ('LE', 'A').
evidence.expected: Wrapped lines inside the drawing area so the table and item cited are legible.

findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the note/summary text to the sheet width.

findings.title: S-103.2/.3 line labels collide with panel-length labels

evidence.measured: S-103.2: 'BWL-W-G-W 24.0' WSP' printed over the panel label at the garage west wall and the S line label beside '29" CS-WSP'; S-103.3: 'BWL-W-A-E1 36.0' WSP' printed on top of the east '53"' panel label. Panel lengths themselves match the model (E1 34.25/42.75/153.5 -> 34/43/154).

findings.proposed_fix: Offset line labels from panel labels.

findings.title: S-101.1 member and beam/post schedules overprint each other

evidence.measured: MEMBER SCHEDULE's QTY/MARK columns run into BEAM / POST SCHEDULE's first column (e.g. 'MARKMARK', span values stacked on mark text) and the HEADER SCHEDULE span/qty values overprint mark text. Header schedule values themselves match the model (D-B-CLOSET/GYM 2-2x8, D-B-PATIO 2-2x10, span = RO + jacks).

findings.proposed_fix: Widen column gap or reflow the three tables.

findings.title: A-532/A-544 stack-shelf dimension strings misplaced or ambiguous

evidence.measured: A-532: dimension '4" CI' is clipped by the foam hatch and '4" XPS (2 layers)' floats ~1 ft below the stack; A-544: '3.5" stud' dimension sits on the upper staggered wall whose layer reads 'staggered-studs 5.5"' (it measures the lower partition stud). Layer depths themselves are right (2x6 plate 5.5, 2x4 stud 3.5).
evidence.expected: Dimension strings adjacent to what they measure.

findings.proposed_fix: Place dimension text on its member; no model change.

findings.title: Openings 3'-6" to 5'-3" wide get only 1 king + 1 jack per side

evidence.measured: king_jack_counts returns (1,1) up to 6 ft: D-M-MUDC 50.24 in. K1/J1, D-B-PLAY 62.35 in. K1/J1, WIN-M-DINING-E 63 in. K1/J1 (2-ply 9.5 in. LVL), 38.24 in. doors K1/J1. 63.31 in. doors get K2/J2 only through their door-pattern jamb_framing.
evidence.expected: Per coordinator's approximate IRC 2021 Table R602.7.5 (<=3 ft 1 king; >3-4 ft 2; >4-8 ft 2) these need 2 kings per side if the wall is bearing/exterior. NOT verified against the table (fetch blocked); applicability depends on wall role and header span, so confidence low.
evidence.method: p6/p7 probes (scratchpad F1/p7.py) list K/J per opening; code read in tables.py.

findings.proposed_fix: Verify the table, then make king_jack_counts depend on span and bearing role; billing and S-101 header schedule would move.
